pages.heading: Move with the foundation to grow
pages.intro: A successful migration makes the estate easier to govern, secure and operate. Quadra starts with dependencies and the target operating model, then selects the right Azure treatment for each workload.

sections.heading: Assess before moving
sections.body: Inventory infrastructure, applications, databases, licensing, performance, security and recovery needs. Group workloads into migration waves by dependency and business risk; agree validation, cutover and rollback criteria before execution.

sections.heading: Establish the landing zone
sections.body: Design or remediate management groups, subscriptions, identity, network connectivity, policy, logging, backup and recovery. Cloud Adoption Framework principles shape guardrails and operational readiness rather than treating the landing zone as an isolated deployment.

sections.heading: Modernise the estate
bullets: Move Windows, Linux, SAP and VMware workloads from on-premises, AWS or Google Cloud to Azure.
Assess SQL Server compatibility and select Azure SQL Database, Managed Instance or SQL on Azure VMs; consider PostgreSQL, MySQL and Cosmos DB where appropriate.
Support Azure Virtual Desktop, Azure Files and Azure NetApp Files, with Azure Arc for hybrid management.
Design connectivity and application access using ExpressRoute, Virtual WAN, Front Door, Application Gateway and WAF.

sections.heading: Validate, optimise and hand over
sections.body: Protect data integrity through validation and planned recovery steps. Tune availability, performance and cost after cutover, and transition monitoring, backup, disaster recovery and operating runbooks into the agreed support model. Well-Architected and FinOps reviews identify the next improvements. Downtime windows and migration methods depend on workload constraints and the agreed sequence.

pages.heading: Unify data. Improve decisions. Put intelligence to work.
pages.intro: Build a governed foundation for analytics and AI with Microsoft Fabric, Azure Databricks, SQL and Microsoft Foundry. Quadra connects data engineering, business context and production operation around a defined problem.

sections.heading: Modernise and connect the data estate
sections.body: Assess databases, warehouses, lakes and legacy reporting. Plan migration from Synapse, Data Factory and other platforms where justified; Fabric and Databricks can complement one another rather than requiring a blanket replacement.

sections.heading: Build the right platform
bullets: Fabric: OneLake, Lakehouse, Warehouse, engineering, semantic models, Power BI, data science and Real-Time Intelligence.
Databricks: scalable ingestion, medallion architecture, transformation, machine learning and platform optimisation.
Analytics and IoT: operational dashboards, streaming data, plant and asset monitoring, predictive insight and event-driven decisions.
AI: retrieval-augmented generation, search, document intelligence and business-process assistants grounded in approved enterprise data.

sections.heading: Engineer trust and day-two operation
sections.body: Purview, catalogue and lineage, access controls and data quality support governance. DataOps and MLOps introduce deployment, testing and environment controls; evaluation, monitoring and security support AI use. Managed services cover platform health, capacity, performance, FinOps and continuous enhancement.

sections.heading: Start with Azure AI Launchpad
sections.body: A focused discovery engagement reviews business pain points, application and data landscapes, analytics maturity and priority use cases. Outputs include readiness observations, architecture options, a proof-of-value recommendation and a phased roadmap. Scope and engagement format are agreed before starting.

sections.heading: Connect to the decisions that matter
sections.body: Explore production and quality visibility, BFSI risk and reporting, pharma operations, retail inventory, IT service analytics or finance and procurement intelligence. Choose success measures with the business owner before building.

sections.heading: Integrate without assuming identical controls
sections.body: Where Fabric and Azure Databricks interoperate, validate the specific mirroring or shortcut pattern, read behaviour and access model. Governance policies must be checked across the participating systems; they should not be assumed to transfer automatically.

FinOps: budgets, allocation, right-sizing, capacity, reservation utilisation and commitment governance.

Agree controls, evidence requirements and remediation owners, then carry the resulting policies and response responsibilities into managed operations.

pages.heading: AWS Security & Governance
pages.intro:
Quadra helps organizations establish a proactive and unified security posture across cloud infrastructure, applications, data, identities, software delivery, and AI workloads.

Security and governance are embedded from the beginning, enabling organizations to innovate with greater confidence while protecting critical information, services, and reputation.

sections.heading: Establish a Governed Foundation
sections.body:
Inconsistent account structures, access models, and policies can create security gaps as cloud adoption grows.

Quadra establishes a governed multi-account foundation with standardized identity, networking, logging, policy controls, and security baselines.
sections.closing_body: Outcomes to work toward: Consistent governance, reduced configuration risk, improved visibility, and secure scaling across business units.

sections.heading: Architect for Defense in Depth
sections.body:
No single security control can protect an entire cloud environment.

Quadra designs layered security across identity, network, workloads, applications, data, logging, monitoring, and recovery. Controls are aligned with workload criticality and business risk.
sections.closing_body: Outcomes to work toward: Reduced attack surface, stronger resilience, better containment, and improved protection of critical assets.

sections.heading: Build Security into Software Delivery
sections.body:
Security assessments performed only after deployment can delay releases and increase remediation costs.

Quadra integrates policy checks, code analysis, dependency validation, infrastructure scanning, secrets protection, and approval controls into development and deployment workflows.
sections.closing_body: Outcomes to work toward: Earlier risk detection, reduced production vulnerabilities, faster secure releases, and improved developer accountability.

sections.heading: Centralize Governance and Compliance
sections.body:
Organizations need continuous visibility into whether cloud resources comply with approved security and regulatory controls.

Quadra establishes centralized policies, control monitoring, evidence collection, exception handling, and remediation workflows across cloud accounts.
sections.closing_body: Outcomes to work toward: Improved compliance readiness, reduced audit effort, better control visibility, and consistent policy enforcement.

sections.heading: Prioritize Security Risk Across the Cloud Estate
sections.body:
A large volume of independent findings can make it difficult to understand which risks require immediate action.

Quadra correlates security signals with asset value, identity exposure, network reachability, vulnerabilities, and data sensitivity to identify the issues that create meaningful business risk.
sections.closing_body: Outcomes to work toward: Faster risk reduction, better remediation prioritization, reduced alert fatigue, and clearer executive reporting.

sections.heading: Detect and Respond to Threats Intelligently
sections.body:
Modern attacks can move across identities, workloads, storage, applications, and networks.

Quadra implements continuous monitoring and intelligent correlation to identify suspicious activity, connect related events, support investigations, and initiate approved response workflows. Monitoring coverage and escalation responsibilities are agreed for the supported environment.
sections.closing_body: Outcomes to work toward: Earlier attack detection, faster containment, reduced investigation effort, and improved incident response.

sections.heading: Protect Applications and Networks
sections.body:
Internet-facing applications, APIs, networks, and remote connectivity remain common targets for exploitation.

Quadra designs layered protections for application traffic, APIs, networks, segmentation, egress, remote access, and distributed workloads.
sections.closing_body: Outcomes to work toward: Reduced external exposure, improved application availability, stronger network control, and better protection against automated attacks.

sections.heading: Modernize Identity and Zero Trust Access
sections.body:
Excessive permissions, unused access, and long-lived credentials can significantly increase security risk.

Quadra establishes identity-first security using centralized workforce access, short-lived credentials, role-based permissions, privileged-access controls, and continuous access review.
sections.closing_body: Outcomes to work toward: Reduced credential risk, improved least-privilege adoption, simplified access governance, and better user accountability.

sections.heading: Protect Data and Encryption Keys
sections.body:
Sensitive data may be distributed across storage, databases, analytics environments, backups, logs, and AI platforms.

Quadra helps organizations discover sensitive information, enforce encryption, govern keys, control access, define retention, and monitor data exposure.
sections.closing_body: Outcomes to work toward: Reduced data-leakage risk, stronger privacy controls, improved key governance, and better compliance readiness.

sections.heading: Secure AI Workloads
sections.body:
AI adoption introduces new risks involving sensitive data exposure, excessive agent permissions, unsafe outputs, untrusted content, prompt manipulation, and uncontrolled actions.

Quadra establishes security controls for AI data access, model usage, agent identities, tool permissions, human approvals, logging, evaluation, and monitoring.
sections.closing_body: Outcomes to work toward: Safer AI adoption, controlled agent behavior, reduced data exposure, and improved accountability for AI-driven actions.

sections.heading: Protect the Software Supply Chain
sections.body:
Applications increasingly depend on open-source packages, third-party components, automated pipelines, and external development tools.

Quadra helps organizations validate dependencies, manage software components, protect build pipelines, secure artifacts, and monitor supply-chain risk.
sections.closing_body: Outcomes to work toward: Reduced dependency risk, improved release integrity, faster vulnerability response, and more secure software delivery.

sections.body:
Security teams can spend significant time collecting context, investigating repetitive findings, and coordinating remediation.

Quadra applies governed security agents to summarize findings, correlate context, prioritize risks, support investigations, recommend remediation, and automate approved response actions.
sections.closing_body: Outcomes to work toward: Faster triage, reduced analyst workload, improved remediation consistency, and more proactive security operations.

pages.heading: Recover the Business—not Just the Backup
pages.intro: Ransomware, accidental change and service failure create different recovery problems. sections.heading: Define the recovery outcome before choosing the tool
sections.body: Start with business impact and dependencies across on-premises, cloud, SaaS, endpoints and AI-enabled workflows. Set an RTO for the time to restore a service and an RPO for acceptable data loss. These are design and test objectives, not guarantees inherited from a product.
bullets: Map applications, data, identities, network services, keys and external dependencies to business owners.

sections.heading: Protect copies. Validate the path back.
sections.body: Design isolation, immutability and access separation around the threat model and supported platform behaviour. A retained copy is useful only if credentials, keys, catalogues and recovery capacity are also available.
bullets: Protect agreed virtual machines, databases, files, cloud-native workloads, SaaS applications, repositories and endpoints.

Use isolated recovery environments where appropriate to test applications, configuration and data before reconnecting to production.
Plan cross-environment recovery and failback where supported, accounting for format, bandwidth, egress, capacity and licensing constraints.

bullets: Evaluate object, configuration, relationship and forest-level recovery separately; providers and products do not offer identical restore granularity.

For AI workloads, identify protected datasets, data lakes, pipelines, model artefacts, configuration and supported workspace content.

Before an AI service resumes, validate data provenance and integrity, permissions, connectors and representative outputs with the AI owner. A successful restore does not by itself make a model trustworthy.
Treat recovery from unwanted agent actions as a scoped application and data problem; not every external transaction can be reversed by restoring a backup.

sections.heading: One recovery plan, explicit decision rights

bullets: Use measured test results to compare achieved recovery with the agreed RTO and RPO.
Keep audit logs, approvals and test records with an agreed evidence-retention policy.
Review unresolved risk, recovery cost and the next improvement actions with business owners.

sections.heading: Scope a resilience readiness assessment

pages.intro: Complex estates can accumulate separate backup policies, recovery tools and ownership gaps. Quadra helps evaluate and implement a Commvault-based design that connects protection, identity dependencies and recovery operations across agreed hybrid, cloud and SaaS workloads—starting with the services the business needs to restore.

sections.heading: Choose the operating model as carefully as the platform
sections.body: Commvault is an OEM technology option for estates seeking a coordinated protection and recovery approach. Compare software, SaaS and appliance delivery, skills, lifecycle responsibilities and workload coverage. For cloud-native AWS requirements, evaluate the role of Clumio by Commvault within the design.
bullets: Assess the Commvault Cloud Unity platform release and its Resilience Ops approach against your protection and recovery priorities.
Agree the release, licence, region, integrations and supported recovery paths for the selected deployment.
Retain specialist tools where workload or control requirements justify them, and consolidate where replacement coverage is proven.

sections.heading: Data protection across the agreed workload estate
sections.body: Build a protection matrix and policy framework for the required workloads, then test representative restores. Coverage is established at workload and object level—not inferred from a broad platform label.
bullets: Virtual machines, databases and file systems across supported on-premises environments.
Cloud-native applications and data on AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud, subject to the relevant service and connector support.
SaaS applications such as Microsoft 365, Google Workspace and Salesforce; DevOps repositories and AI data where supported.
Isolated and immutable copies with retention, administrator separation and recovery-access requirements explicitly configured.

sections.heading: Recover the application context as well as its data
sections.body: Application configurations and cloud infrastructure may be needed alongside the protected data. Define how incident findings inform recovery-point selection, where restoration occurs and who approves reconnection.
bullets: Evaluate Threat Scan and clean-point identification to investigate compromised data and select a candidate recovery point.
Assess Synthetic Recovery for supported selective recovery scenarios; establish what can be excluded, reconstructed or restored.
Evaluate an on-demand Commvault Cleanroom for isolated recovery testing, investigation and validation, with capacity, connectivity and evidence access defined.
Test supported cross-cloud, cross-hypervisor or cleanroom recovery paths and the route back to production.
sections.closing_body: Combine scanning and isolation with application checks and security approval before reconnecting recovered services.

sections.heading: Protect the systems that control access
sections.body: Map Tier 0 identity dependencies, the most privileged assets and the people or services that control them. Scope supported Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID recovery around the objects, permissions and dependencies needed to restore business access. The design specifies the recovery method for each identity provider and workload.
bullets: Identify the identity, permission and access-change evidence needed to investigate an incident and choose a recovery point.
Map privileged exposure and emergency access with the directory and security owners.
For organisations exploring broader identity resilience, scope a separate evaluation of cross-provider auditing, guided remediation and configuration rollback.
Define object-level and wider directory-recovery requirements separately, then test the selected supported paths and prerequisites.
sections.closing_body: This is an identity-recovery workstream. Microsoft-specific security architecture and controls remain with Microsoft Security; directory owners approve restoration and access changes.

sections.heading: Know sensitive data—and who or what can reach it
sections.body: Evaluate discovery and classification of sensitive and personal information across supported data stores and applications. Connect findings to protection policy and access decisions for people and AI. Where broader access governance is needed, assess the required integrations as a separate workstream with the responsible data and security owners.
bullets: Assess AI-assisted classification and policy recommendations against representative customer data.
Define the scope of data and AI access monitoring and enforcement, including the systems where controls actually apply.
Evaluate identity, access and data anomaly signals, together with supported third-party threat-intelligence integrations.
sections.closing_body: Coordinate non-Microsoft data-security controls with Enterprise Cybersecurity, Microsoft controls with Microsoft Security and AI lifecycle decisions with Enterprise AI Engineering.

sections.heading: Resilience without an untested cost assumption
sections.body: Compare the cost and operating effort of consolidation with the existing estate. Include licensing, retained data, infrastructure, cloud consumption, egress, recovery environments, support and migration. Native snapshot management and cloud cost visibility can inform the assessment where supported.
bullets: Evaluate automation and the Arlie assistant for configuration, troubleshooting and recovery guidance, with appropriate access and approval gates.
Measure operator effort and recovery-test outcomes in a scoped pilot rather than carrying vendor TCO comparisons into the business case as a promise.
Keep tool retirement and any claimed savings conditional on validated replacement coverage.

sections.heading: Keep AI data recoverable before putting it to further use
sections.body: Scope protection for data lakes, pipelines, model artefacts and the configuration or infrastructure needed to recreate an AI service. Immutability and isolation protect retained copies; application and AI owners still need to validate data integrity, permissions and model behaviour after restoration.
bullets: Assess poisoning and machine-identity attack scenarios with the security and AI teams; backup alone does not detect or resolve every AI threat.
If reuse of protected data for analytics or AI is a priority, scope a separate evaluation of classification, export formats and the receiving data platform.
Apply purpose, consent, retention and access checks before reusing backup data; a protected copy is not automatic permission to train or analyse.

Metallic AI is Commvault Cloud’s AI and automation layer; Arlie is its AI assistant. Evaluate supported detection, recovery-orchestration and guidance workflows with appropriate permissions, approvals and feature-availability checks.

sections.heading: What a scoped engagement produces
sections.body: Agree a workload and dependency matrix, platform and deployment comparison, policy design, recovery sequence, pilot and test record, operating runbooks and a commercial model. Test the selected recovery paths against service-specific RTO and RPO objectives. Managed delivery is defined through agreed coverage, service hours, customer approvals and escalation—not by the breadth of the OEM portfolio.
bullets: Bring current Commvault entitlements or the replacement scope, the critical-service list and recent recovery findings.
Use the results to decide what to consolidate, what to retain and which recovery gaps to address first.

pages.heading: Turn Protected Data into a Tested Recovery Plan
pages.intro: A backup platform must support the recovery path your business actually needs. Quadra evaluates Veeam for virtualised, hybrid, cloud and SaaS environments, connecting workload protection and recovery orchestration with the data-risk, privacy and governance requirements of the engagement.

sections.heading: Start with protection and recovery requirements
sections.body: Evaluate Veeam Data Platform against supported workloads, restore granularity, deployment choices and operational responsibilities. Compare cloud, Kubernetes, SaaS, on-premises and identity needs individually. Portability can broaden recovery options, but formats, application dependencies, licences and destination capacity still matter.
bullets: Use Veeam Data Platform as the starting point for the backup and recovery design.
For broader data-security or AI-governance needs, scope a separate evaluation of relationship visibility, access controls and integration with existing tools.
Document the selected edition, supported workloads, connectors and recovery destinations in the solution scope.

sections.heading: Find and prioritise data exposure
sections.body: Assess data security posture management requirements across supported cloud, SaaS and on-premises data. Sensitive-data discovery and classification should lead to a prioritised remediation plan with clear control owners.
bullets: Identify public links, excessive permissions, over-sharing and combinations of exposure that increase business risk.
Prioritise findings by data sensitivity, business impact and the practical remediation path.
Use threat-detection and malware-scanning evidence to inform investigation, recovery-point selection and restored-service validation.

sections.heading: Control how people and AI use protected information
sections.body: For organisations extending their resilience programme into AI governance, a separately scoped assessment can define the inventory, access controls and recovery evidence needed. Work with the established governance team to choose appropriate tools and integrations before implementation.
bullets: Define visibility requirements for sanctioned and previously unknown agents, copilots and models, including the telemetry and connectors needed.
Establish how permission drift will be identified and how identity and data owners make least-privilege decisions.
Evaluate data-layer policy enforcement for the required applications, users and machine identities.
Map recovery from unwanted AI actions, including application state, external transactions and downstream effects that need separate remediation.
sections.closing_body: Enterprise AI Engineering remains the route for AI lifecycle and governance. Coordinate Microsoft controls with Microsoft Security and non-Microsoft cyber controls with Enterprise Cybersecurity.

sections.heading: Make privacy requirements part of the data design
sections.body: Map personal and sensitive data to the systems, users and locations involved. Assess policies by data type, role and jurisdiction with the customer’s privacy and legal owners; residency is a design requirement, not a property inferred from a platform name.
bullets: Document data location, transfers, retention and restore destinations.
Evaluate jurisdiction-aware policy support against the actual licence and integrations.
Review redundant, obsolete and trivial data for minimisation, preserving required retention and legal holds before authorising deletion.

sections.heading: Generate evidence that supports—not replaces—assurance
sections.body: Assess automated checks, reports and control mappings against the organisation’s applicable obligations. Requirements may include GDPR, HIPAA, DORA and the EU AI Act, alongside frameworks such as NIST and the AI RMF. A scoped Quadra advisory workstream can review mapping to India’s DPDP Act and relevant RBI, SEBI or IRDAI expectations. The customer’s advisers determine applicability and legal interpretation; platform evidence supports their compliance review.
bullets: Map each required control to the evidence available in the selected product and release.
Evaluate hardened immutability and four-eyes approval for supported changes, with separation of duties and emergency procedures.

Assess Veeam Recovery Orchestrator for supported vSphere, Hyper-V and Azure recovery targets, subject to edition and release eligibility. Plan isolated test environments, capacity and production safeguards.
Retain test results, approvals, exceptions and remediation evidence for the agreed review process.

sections.heading: Recover at the granularity the incident requires
sections.body: Choose recovery methods according to the damaged service, available restore points and validated application dependencies. A granular restore may be appropriate for an object or configuration problem; an infrastructure or identity compromise may require a wider recovery sequence.
bullets: Configure immutable protection where supported and evaluate pre-restore malware scanning with the security responders.
Test precise object- or data-level restores as well as the full service-recovery path.

Veeam Data Platform v13.1 introduces guided Active Directory forest recovery. Confirm the selected edition, prerequisites, access and supported automation; test the directory recovery sequence rather than treating every edition or release as equivalent.
Where appropriate, assess Coveware by Veeam for separately scoped cyber-extortion incident-response support, eligibility and escalation.
sections.closing_body: Test restoration times against the agreed recovery objectives, using representative data volumes, infrastructure, connectivity and application-validation steps.

sections.heading: Build the evidence before selecting the scope
sections.body: A scoped engagement can produce the workload and support matrix, protection policy, dependency-led recovery plan, identity-recovery prerequisites, test evidence and operating runbooks. Compare licensing, storage, cloud use, egress, test capacity, migration and support costs. Establish achieved RTO and RPO results through representative exercises.
bullets: Bring your Veeam estate or target workloads, retention requirements and the incidents or tests that exposed recovery gaps.
Define customer-operated, co-managed or managed responsibilities, service hours, approvals and escalation in the commercial scope.
Expand into data security, privacy or AI-related features only when their support and cross-practice ownership have been established.

pages.heading: SaaS-Led Resilience for a Distributed Enterprise
pages.intro: Managing backup infrastructure can distract teams from the harder question: can the business recover? Quadra evaluates Druva for SaaS-led protection across supported cloud, data-centre, endpoint, SaaS and identity workloads, with recovery, preservation and customer responsibilities designed into the service.

sections.heading: Reduce infrastructure administration—not accountability
sections.body: Druva Resilience Cloud is a SaaS-led technology candidate for the resilience design. A provider-managed backup service changes infrastructure and lifecycle responsibilities; the customer still needs appropriate access, supported connectors or agents, workload onboarding, network capacity, policies and a tested restore path.
bullets: Confirm supported workloads, tenant configuration, licensing, available regions and permitted recovery destinations.
Evaluate Dru MetaGraph and related intelligence capabilities against current availability and the data or relationships they actually cover.
Compare provider-managed infrastructure with customer-operated alternatives using whole-life costs and recovery requirements.

sections.heading: Recover, govern, defend and enable AI—within a tested scope
sections.body: AI services can change data and application state faster than traditional recovery procedures anticipate. Establish the objects, content and permissions available for backup and restoration before claiming protection of an AI workspace.

cards.title: Recover
cards.body: Evaluate recovery from unwanted autonomous actions at the supported data or configuration level. Validate dependencies and downstream consequences; not all actions can be reversed.

cards.title: Govern
cards.body: Evaluate supported Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts, responses and generated files. For Claude, scope protection to Claude Code and Cowork data on managed Windows and macOS endpoints; Claude.ai cloud chat history is outside this protection scope. Confirm supported files, retention and restoration granularity.

cards.title: Defend
cards.body: Review backup administration, access separation, anomaly signals and response procedures against AI-enabled attacks as part of the wider security programme.

cards.title: Enable
cards.body: Evaluate DruAI and Druva MCP for connecting approved AI assistants to backup and recovery intelligence. Define least-privilege access, allowed actions, human approvals and audit records.

sections.closing_body: Scope the supported AI content, integrations and recovery actions for the selected service. Coordinate AI lifecycle and restart decisions with Enterprise AI Engineering.

sections.heading: Protect distributed business data
sections.body: Evaluate Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Salesforce, VMware, endpoint and cloud-workload protection against the supported service and object matrix. SaaS-led scaling can reduce backup-infrastructure administration; onboarding time and recovery performance still depend on the workload, connectivity and configuration.
bullets: Protect agreed business-critical laptop and desktop data, including the recovery and retention needs of departed employees.

Select regions and data flows according to the chosen workload and service availability, residency obligations and recovery destinations. Region support varies by workload; a portfolio-wide count does not establish availability for a particular application.
Model licence, retained capacity, data transfer, recovery, implementation and operational costs against the existing environment. Validate savings rather than applying a vendor percentage.

sections.heading: Recover the identity foundation in the right order
sections.body: Evaluate Druva Identity Resilience for Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID and Okta protection, including supported forest-level recovery. The offering uses Enterprise per-user licensing; confirm entitlements and supported objects for each provider. Map directory and authentication dependencies to the business recovery plan, including privileged access and emergency credentials.
bullets: Active Directory: assess granular object restore and guided forest-level recovery, with domain-controller availability and the supported recovery procedure tested before commitment.
Microsoft Entra ID: confirm which users, groups, roles, memberships and relationships can be restored and what dependencies or exclusions apply.
Okta: validate the supported identity configurations, objects and restoration sequence.
Security: review encryption in transit and at rest, key-management responsibilities, administrative access and recovery prerequisites for the selected service.
sections.closing_body: Backup and recovery of a Microsoft identity workload does not move Microsoft Security ownership into HCDW. The directory owner and Microsoft Security specialists remain part of the recovery and control decisions.

sections.heading: Use recovery evidence to narrow uncertainty
sections.body: Establish what incident responders can learn from logs, changed-data visibility, proactive detection and threat-hunting tools. Feed that evidence into recovery-point selection and an authorised, isolated validation process.
bullets: Configure isolation and immutability with the appropriate retention and administrative boundaries.
Evaluate anomaly detection and threat hunting across supported backups for indicators of compromise.
Select a candidate last-known-good snapshot using available evidence, then validate restored data and services before reconnecting.
Define how investigation, containment and recovery handoffs work with the security responders.
sections.closing_body: Document the evidence behind the selected recovery point and complete the agreed security and business acceptance checks before service restart.

sections.heading: Make preservation and eDiscovery defensible
sections.body: Assess whether existing backups can support authorised collection, preservation and investigation for the required endpoint and SaaS data. The legal owner defines the matter, custodians, preservation obligations and release authority.
bullets: Legal hold: evaluate preservation across supported endpoints and SaaS sources, including exclusions from ordinary deletion and the release workflow.
Federated search: validate files, versions, deleted items and departed-employee data against the retained and indexed content.
Evidence integrity: review audit trails, chain-of-custody records and alignment with the organisation’s Electronic Discovery Reference Model (EDRM) process.
Compliance monitoring: assess relevant GDPR, HIPAA and PCI templates and supported eDiscovery integrations such as Exterro.
sections.closing_body: A backup and an audit log are inputs to a defensible process, not automatic proof of admissibility or compliance. Collection scope, integrity checks, access and legal review still matter.

sections.heading: Define the service you will actually operate
sections.body: A scoped engagement can produce the workload and object matrix, residency and data-flow design, retention and hold policies, identity-recovery sequence, restore-test evidence and operating runbooks. Confirm the selected features and integrations with the OEM before committing the design.
bullets: Compare achieved recovery timings and data currency with the agreed RTO and RPO objectives.
Agree how Druva’s service, Quadra’s managed delivery and the customer’s administrators share responsibilities, service hours and escalation.
Bring your distributed workforce, SaaS and identity priorities to scope a pilot or assessment with defined outputs and commercial terms.

sections.heading: Do not use an agent where a rule will do
sections.body: Understand the workflow, its exceptions and its business objective first. Use predictable automation for defined rules; introduce AI for tasks that benefit from reasoning or unstructured information. Human review belongs at decisions that require accountability.

sections.heading: Integrate the enterprise
sections.body: Connect work across SAP, ServiceNow, Salesforce, Oracle, Microsoft 365, Databricks and Power Platform. IntelliLink and approved connectors or APIs provide integration patterns; the implementation follows supported interfaces, permissions and the customer environment.

Industry-specific processes: define the workflow, systems of record and governance requirements before selecting the technical pattern.

sections.heading: Make progress measurable
sections.body: Establish the baseline, measurement period and method before rollout. Evaluate the resulting work, exceptions and control behaviour rather than treating an activity count as business value. Move from an initial cohort to wider use with adoption and expansion criteria, then feed production learning into managed AI and governance reviews.

pages.heading: Give enterprise AI clear boundaries and accountable owners
pages.intro:
Governance belongs in the architecture before the first production release.

sections.heading: Define what each system may do
sections.body: Establish who can use an agent, which data and tools it may access, and where human approval is mandatory. Maintain policy boundaries across model choices, integrations and business channels rather than relying on a model’s answer alone.

sections.heading: Four connected governance domains
bullets: Identity and policy: roles, permissions, tool access and approval requirements.
Evaluation and observability: quality, behaviour, drift, exceptions and performance evidence.
Lifecycle and cost: deployment, change, improvement, retirement and spend governance.
Compliance evidence: an inventory, traceability, monitoring and control documentation aligned to the relevant use case.

sections.heading: Connect governance to engineering and operation
sections.body: IntelliAssure provides an assurance context for reviewing production readiness; managed AI carries evaluation and improvement into operation. Management-system principles inform controls. Map relevant DPDPA and EU AI Act requirements with the customer’s governance and legal teams according to role, jurisdiction and use case.

sections.heading: Connect governance and security
sections.body: Connect enterprise AI governance with specialist cybersecurity and Microsoft Security expertise. BluForge IntelliGuard is a unified AI-powered security operations and cyber resilience platform. Agree how governance findings, security signals and response responsibilities connect across the operating teams.
